codex: Every part is edible — leaves, flowers, roots. Bitter means nutritious. The first green of spring and the last of fall.
lookalikeNote: Unmistakable once flowering. Young rosette leaves are the safest stage.
name: Dandelion
preparation: Eat raw; boil to reduce bitterness. Roots can be roasted.

codex: The survivalist's supermarket: shoots, roots, pollen, and fluff for tinder. If you find cattails, you found water too.
lookalikeNote: Distinctive brown hot-dog head is unmistakable. Harvest shoots before the head forms.
name: Cattail
preparation: Peel young shoots, eat raw or boiled. Roots pounded for starch.

codex: Fall's candy. The fruit sweetens after frost — nature's own ripening timer. Dries well for winter stores.
lookalikeNote: Wait for the frost-softened fruit. If it puckers your mouth inside out, it wasn't ready.

preparation: Eat only fully ripe (soft, wrinkled). Unripe = mouthful of chalk.

codex: The staple that fed nations. Tannins must be leached or they'll punish you — but leached acorn meal is flour. Flour is bread. Bread is winter.
lookalikeNote: Stick to white oak group (rounded lobe tips). Red oak acorns need far more leaching.
name: White Oak Acorns
preparation: MUST leach: shell, grind, soak in running water until bitterness is gone. White oak group is mildest.

name: Wild Onion
